title: Pollo al Ajillo
subtitle: Spanish garlic chicken braised in white wine and sherry
excerpt: Pollo al ajillo is the definitive Spanish garlic chicken: bone-in chicken pieces fried in olive oil with a large amount of garlic, then braised with white wine and a splash of sherry. The garlic softens and sweetens as it cooks, and the pan juices become a glossy, intensely garlicky sauce. It is one of the most universally made dishes in Spain.
sourceNotes: Pollo al ajillo (garlic chicken) is one of the most widely prepared Spanish dishes, made in every region and found in every tapas bar and home kitchen. The dish reflects the Spanish love of garlic used in generous quantities. The addition of sherry is associated with Andalusia, but the dish is made across Spain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves if made a day ahead.

content.text: Use a whole head of garlic -- around 10 to 12 cloves. The garlic is left whole or halved, not crushed. It fries in the oil alongside the chicken and turns sweet and sticky as it softens. Do not let the garlic burn at the start: add it to the hot oil before the chicken and watch it carefully.
Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a wide heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{garlic}} garlic cloves and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until starting to turn golden. Remove and set aside.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Season {{chicken-thigh}} chicken with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Brown on both sides, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Return the garlic to the pan with {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves and {{chilli-flakes}} chilli flakes (if using).

Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and {{sherry-dry}} sherry. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for a further 10 minutes to reduce and concentrate the sauce. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over and serve with crusty bread or rice.

items.symptom: The garlic burned at the start
items.cause: The oil was too hot when the garlic went in.
items.fix: Start with medium heat, not high. The garlic should sizzle gently and turn golden slowly over 2 to 3 minutes. If it browns too fast, reduce the heat. Burned garlic makes the sauce bitter.

content.text: Pollo al ajillo is made across the whole of Spain. Every family has a version. In Madrid it is made with the thighs and drumsticks; in Andalusia a splash of sherry goes in with the wine; in Castile it is cooked without wine at all, just garlic and olive oil. The dish is also one of the most popular tapas bar dishes in Spain, served in small portions with bread to mop up the garlic oil.
